argument: When many parameter settings fit the training data, initialization, optimizer, step size, parameterization, and training schedule select a particular solution. Gradient methods can favor max-margin or low-norm solutions in some regimes, acting as implicit regularizers without an explicit penalty.
boundary: Known characterizations often assume linear, separable, homogeneous, or simplified models.
The implicit bias can change under reparameterization and adaptive optimizers.
Low norm in parameter space need not imply causal or distributional robustness.

interpretation: Principia should treat training procedure as part of the model. Two systems with identical architectures can embody different Principles because their optimization paths differ.
